name: Cypriot Kleftiko
description: Kleftiko genuinely means 'stolen meat' - the name traces back to Cypriot bandits (klephts) who stole livestock and cooked it sealed in underground earth ovens specifically to trap the smoke and avoid detection. Real technique still depends on that same real seal: the lamb, marinated in garlic, lemon, and herbs, is wrapped or covered tightly so no moisture escapes, then cooked low and slow for eight hours or more, until it's genuinely fall-off-the-bone tender.
steps_detailed: Rub the lamb with the garlic, lemon juice, and oregano, and let marinate at least 30 minutes, ideally overnight.
Place the lamb and potato in a baking dish with the bay leaf, and cover tightly with foil, sealing the edges well so no moisture or steam escapes - this real seal is the entire point of kleftiko.
Bake at 300F (150C) for 3-3.5 hours without removing the foil, until the meat is genuinely fall-apart tender.
Uncover for the last 15 minutes to let the top brown lightly.

name: Cypriot Halloumi Souvlaki
description: Halloumi souvlaki showcases Cyprus's real national cheese - real halloumi's genuinely high melting point means it holds its shape on the grill rather than melting, developing a real char outside while staying firm inside; it's best served immediately, hot, when its real squeaky texture is most pronounced.
steps_detailed: Toss the halloumi with the olive oil, lemon juice, garlic, and oregano, and marinate 15-20 minutes.
Thread onto skewers alternating with the bell pepper.
Grill over medium-high heat, turning, 6-8 minutes, until charred outside - real halloumi holds its shape rather than melting.
Serve immediately while hot.

name: Cypriot Village Salad (Horiatiki)
description: Horiatiki, a real Cypriot village salad, is genuinely built on ripe tomatoes, cucumber, and real feta or halloumi, dressed simply with olive oil, real technique using a light hand with the dressing so the vegetables' own flavor carries the dish.
steps_detailed: Toss the tomatoes, cucumber, onion, and olives with the olive oil and oregano.
Top with a slab of feta rather than crumbling it in.

name: Cypriot Moussaka
description: Moussaka, Cyprus's layered eggplant and spiced meat dish topped with real béchamel, real technique salting the eggplant first to draw out bitterness before layering.
steps_detailed: Salt the eggplant slices and let sit 15 minutes, then pat dry and roast at 425F (220C) for 15-18 minutes.
Brown the lamb, add the tomatoes, and simmer 15 minutes.
Melt the butter, whisk in the flour, cook 1 minute, then gradually whisk in the milk until thickened into a béchamel.
Layer the roasted eggplant and meat sauce in a baking dish, top with the béchamel, and bake at 375F (190C) for 30-35 minutes until golden.

name: Cypriot Souvlaki (Pork)
description: Souvlaki, skewered grilled meat, is a beloved Cypriot street food staple, real technique marinating overnight so the lemon and oregano genuinely penetrate the meat.
steps_detailed: Marinate the beef in the lemon juice, olive oil, oregano, and garlic for at least 2 hours, ideally overnight.
Thread onto skewers.
Grill over medium-high heat, turning, 10-12 minutes, until charred and cooked through.

name: Cypriot Fried Halloumi with Lemon
description: Fried halloumi with a simple squeeze of lemon lets the cheese's own real flavor and texture speak for itself, a beloved simple Cypriot way to eat it.
steps_detailed: Pan-fry the halloumi slices with no added oil, 2-3 minutes per side, until golden and slightly softened inside.
Squeeze the lemon juice over and sprinkle with oregano.
Serve immediately while hot.

name: Cypriot Tzatziki
description: Tzatziki, a cold yogurt and cucumber dip, is the real, traditional accompaniment to kleftiko and souvlaki, real technique salting the cucumber first to draw out excess water.
steps_detailed: Salt the grated cucumber and let sit 10 minutes, then squeeze out excess water.
Whisk the yogurt with the garlic and olive oil, then stir in the cucumber.
Chill at least 20 minutes before serving.

steps_detailed: Rub the fish with the garlic and lemon juice, and let sit 10 minutes.
Grill or broil, 4-5 minutes per side, until just cooked through.

steps_detailed: Toast the almonds in a dry pan over medium heat, stirring often, 4-5 minutes, until fragrant.
